title: Polite Requests: Can I have...? / I'd like...
description: Learn how to order food and drink politely in a cafe or restaurant using standard formulas.
objectives: Use 'Can I have...?' and 'Could I have...?' for courteous requests
Use 'I would like...' and its contraction 'I'd like...' naturally
Include polite markers ('please', 'thank you', 'excuse me') at appropriate stages of service

sections.title: Polite Cafe Ordering Formulas
sections.content:
In English-speaking culture, asking for food bluntly (*'I want tea'*) sounds rude or demanding. Instead, use these **polite formulas**:

### 1. 'Can I have...?' / 'Could I have...?'
- *Can I have a cup of tea, please?*
- *Could I have a bottle of water, please?* (Even more polite)

### 2. 'I would like...' -> 'I'd like...'
- *I'd like a chicken sandwich, please.*
- *I'd like two coffees to take away.*

### 3. Paying the Bill
- *Can we have the bill, please?* (UK) / *Check, please.* (US)

callouts.title: Always Include 'Please'
callouts.text: In English service encounters, adding **please** at the end of every order is not just polite—it is expected social etiquette.

callouts.title: Avoid 'I Want'
callouts.text: Never say 'I want' to a waiter. Say **I would like** or **Can I have**.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
sections.content: Cafe and restaurant polite ordering summary:
summaryPoints: Use 'Can I have...?' or 'Could I have...?' for courteous requests.
Use 'I'd like...' (I would like) instead of 'I want'.
Always add 'please' to orders and 'thank you' when receiving items.
Know the options: 'For here' (eat in) vs 'To take away' (carry out).
Ask for the check/bill with: 'Can we have the bill, please?'.
